description: Inspect or explicitly manage a repository's host schedule.

commands.usage:
usage: orchid service install [--repo <path>] [--interval-s <seconds>] [--dry-run]
Install or replace this repository's schedule after unattended trust is acknowledged. --repo defaults to ORCHID_REPO or the current directory; interval defaults to pump_interval_s (240). --dry-run renders and places inert schedule files and prints scheduler commands, without installing the schedule.

usage: orchid service uninstall [--repo <path>] [--dry-run]
Remove exactly the schedule bound to this repository. An absent schedule is a successful no-op. --repo defaults to ORCHID_REPO or the current directory; --dry-run previews without removing.

usage: orchid service status [--repo <path>] [--dry-run]
Inspect the exact schedule bound to this repository. --repo defaults to ORCHID_REPO or the current directory; --dry-run prints host-query commands without running them.

usage: orchid service teardown [--repo <path>] [--force] [--dry-run]
Uninstall the repository's schedule and only then remove its linked integration worktree. --force applies only to git worktree remove, never scheduler ownership or unload safety; --dry-run removes nothing.

usage: orchid service help
Show schedule-management reference. Equivalent to orchid service --help.

notes:
Inspect or explicitly manage a repository's host schedule. Install requires orchid trust unattended <repo> --reason "<reason>". Install and uninstall are idempotent; install idempotence is about the SAME path. A moved checkout must uninstall its original binding before reinstalling. Binding records must agree and identify the actual owner; copies and edited identities are refused before scheduler or file changes.

TEARDOWN ORDERING: uninstall the service FIRST, then remove the integration worktree, as ONE conditional operation: orchid service teardown --repo <path>. A refused uninstall leaves the worktree intact. If doing the two steps yourself, run from the main checkout: orchid service uninstall --repo <path> && git worktree remove <path>. A schedule remains installed after a run finishes; inspect service status or doctor for the bound state and leftover schedule.
